clue.text: Grouse shooting imminent, so surrender!

definitions.meaning: read literally: the game birds are up and about to be shot, grouse being game
a cry admitting one has been caught out and must give in

explanation.surface: A warning to give in, as the grouse season is about to open.
explanation.walkthrough: Grouse are game birds shot in Britain from August; read literally, the phrase says the game is up, ready for the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when a deception is exposed and one must concede, so it serves as a call to give in.

clue.text: Heading for penitentiary and walls of Rochester, is one inside?

definitions.text: Heading for penitentiary and walls of Rochester, is one inside?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so take the start of penitentiary
inside says the words is one sit within those outer letters
the walls of a word are its outer letters, the first and last of Rochester

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bound for jail behind the walls of Rochester asks whether one is in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of a convict: one who is inside, heading for the penitentiary.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is literally one who is inside a jail, so the whole question describes an inmate.

clue.text: What's left, say, delicate outlines

indicators.note: outlines is read as surrounds, so the word for delicate wraps round the other piece

parts.note: delicate fabric or work can be lacy
say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A description of what remains, with fine, delicate outlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlines' reads as a noun but works as a verb: the delicate word outlines, or surrounds, the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is what is left to someone in a will.

clue.text: Heavy person appearing chubby, topless

indicators.note: topless says remove the top letter, the first one, of the synonym

parts.note: plump is a synonym of chubby

explanation.surface: A heavy person shows up looking chubby and bare-chested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the P from PLUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A big, heavy, clumsy person can be called a great lump.

clue.text: Useless, as no dates available?

definitions.meaning: read as a tree or diary that bears no dates, dates being a fruit

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is pointless because there are no dates free.
explanation.walkthrough: Dates are fruit as well as calendar entries; a date palm with none is bearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort that bears no fruit is barren and achieves nothing, hence useless.

clue.text: Stumble round run, as peacock

indicators.note: round says the word for stumble surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to stutter is to stumble over words
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Something trips its way round a course, like a peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts R inside STUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacock is the classic example of a bird that parades proudly, so a swaggering show-off is called one.

clue.text: Scrubber blushing deeply, I'm held face down

indicators.note: held says that piece is kept inside the colour word

parts.note: puce is the dark red of a deep blush

indicators.note: in a down clue, face down says the piece is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cleaner, flushed red, says she is pinned face down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrubber' is the definition, a pumice stone for scrubbing skin, not an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanic stone used to scrub hard skin is a scrubber in the literal sense.

clue.text: Cry of exhilaration, as primitive invention almost finished

indicators.note: almost finished says the word stops one letter short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the wheel is the archetypal early invention

explanation.surface: A whoop of joy as some early invention nears completion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost finished' drops the L from WHEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of delight, as on a fairground ride.

clue.text: Pantomime character left in hurry, one of five

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation sits inside the word for hurry

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, hurry
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A pantomime figure leaves in a rush, one of five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside HARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The diamond-suited clown of commedia dell'arte is a stock figure of the British pantomime harlequinade.

clue.text: Climax in excitement — pity it hurts!

indicators.note: the climax of a word is taken as its end, the last letter of excitement

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity, as in ruthless

explanation.surface: Someone at the peak of excitement complains that it hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying that this always hurts; 'ruth' survives in ruthless.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says honesty of this kind hurts, so the clue's exclamation stands in for it.

clue.text: In space, slate becomes light

indicators.note: In at the start says the word for slate goes inside the word for space

parts.note: a gap is a space
to slate is to criticise harshly, to slam

explanation.surface: In a gap, a roof slate turns into a source of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' means criticise, not the roofing stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An old street lamp burning gas is a kind of light.

clue.text: Normal procedure in accessing course

indicators.note: accessing is read as getting into, so the word in sits inside the word for course

parts.note: a route is a course
taken as written

explanation.surface: A standard practice for getting onto a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A set, regular way of doing things is a usual procedure.

clue.text: Notes for a talker?

parts.note: banknotes, in the saying that cash talks, are what does the talking

explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are cash, and the proverb has cash speak, so it is a talker made of notes.

clue.text: Silver birch almost gold, this with an orange flavour

parts.note: silver means coins, loose change

indicators.note: almost says drop the last letter of the word for birch

parts.note: a birch is a tree
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A silver birch nearly golden, with orange tints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver birch' reads as one tree but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This French liqueur is flavoured with orange peel.

clue.text: Jack Sprat's wife would always gossip

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean, so she ate the fatty parts

explanation.surface: Jack Sprat's wife never stopped gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is a nursery rhyme husband who ate only lean meat while his wife ate only the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for chatting idly literally describes eating fatty meat.

clue.text: Lacking restrictions as ill-prepared picnickers, might you say?

definitions.text: as ill-prepared picnickers, might you say?
definitions.meaning: picnickers who forgot the basket are without a hamper

explanation.surface: Unrestricted, like picnickers who came without preparing.
explanation.walkthrough: A hamper is a wicker picnic basket; picnickers without one are, read as a pun, un-hampered.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to hinder, so the negative means free of hindrance.

clue.text: Hard up when paying for sadomasochism?

definitions.meaning: read as being tied up with straps in exchange for money

explanation.surface: Broke from paying for kinky pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: Strapped in the literal sense is bound with straps; in the idiom it means short.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of funds is the everyday meaning of this idiom.

clue.text: Instrument just beat through pieces of glass

indicators.note: through says the word for just beat runs inside the word for glass pieces

parts.note: panes are pieces of window glass
to pip is to beat narrowly

explanation.surface: A musical instrument barely beating its way through glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just beat' means beat by a whisker, not merely a rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: These reed pipes bound in a row, linked with the god Pan, form a wind instrument.

clue.text: New area isn't? Well, it could be?

indicators.note: new says the letters of area and isn't are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: used as written
used as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An argument about whether a new area is or isn't, and a well it could be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges AREA ISNT. The definition is adjectival: a well could be of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A well under natural pressure that rises without pumping is the kind named, so a well could be this.

clue.text: Such may be the depression of delivery holding Brown back

indicators.note: holding says the word for delivery contains the other piece

parts.note: postal means to do with mail delivery

indicators.note: back says the colour word is read in reverse

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Depression after giving birth, while keeping a brown baby back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests childbirth but is the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Depression after childbirth is a recognised condition named with this adjective.

clue.text: Rabble, one reveals?

definitions.meaning: a disorderly or worthless bunch, in British slang
read literally as one who shows something

explanation.surface: A mob, one of whom is exposing something.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a useless crowd is called this; the second reading splits it as SHOW-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word to dismiss a disorganised group as a rabble.

clue.text: Quiet, stomach, quiet!

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
tum is a stomach

explanation.surface: Telling one's rumbling stomach to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Yiddish and means keeping silent.
explanation.definitionFit: This Yiddish loan word means silent, as in keeping one's mouth shut.

clue.text: Wet around lake — wet!

indicators.note: around says the word for wet goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: soppy means feeble, wet

explanation.surface: Soaked all round the lake, and soaked again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L inside SOPPY. Both 'wet's mean feeble and also literally damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaking or watery, like a puddle-filled floor, is wet.

clue.text: Compound union member's restraining order

indicators.note: restraining says the bride holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a bride is a member of a marriage union; the 's stands for is
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A trade unionist is subject to a restraining order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union but is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a chemical compound of bromine.

clue.text: Third of February, what a child should learn is, it's freezing!

indicators.note: third of says take the third letter of February

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are a child's basics

explanation.surface: On the third of February, a child learns how cold it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; the answer is the shivering noise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the noise of shivering, said when it is very cold.

clue.text: Extremity overly sore at first, entering relationship

parts.note: too means overly

indicators.note: entering says that letter goes inside the word for relationship

parts.note: a tie is a bond or relationship

indicators.note: at first says take the opening letter of sore

explanation.surface: An extremely sore extremity gets caught up in a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts S inside TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for a toe, which is an extremity of the body.

clue.text: Sweet — or not?

definitions.meaning: a sweet, as a pastry dessert

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is sweet or not.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a pastry pudding and sharp-tasting, so it is sweet and not sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a sweet pastry and a sharp, sour taste.

clue.text: Old official partial to free verse

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old official who likes unrhymed poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' looks like a liking but signals a part of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval local administrator or magistrate in England held this office.

clue.text: Vehicle opening in reverse onto a part of motorway

indicators.note: in reverse says the word for opening is read backwards

parts.note: a pore is a small opening
a lane is part of a motorway

explanation.surface: A vehicle reverses onto part of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns PORE into EROP, which is placed onto A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is a flying vehicle.
